notes:
Renault Zoe phase 2, read over the diagnostic CAN on the OBD-II socket at 500 kbit/s with UDS. The addressing is mixed: 19 units use 11-bit identifiers and 8 (ABS-VDC, battery charger, E-ACT-EBA, INV-ME, both battery controllers, the security gateway and the vehicle control module) use 29-bit identifiers of the form 18DA<target><source>, ISO 15765-4 29-bit normal fixed addressing, which is how CanZE and the ddt4all table list them. The bus setting is the 11-bit default and each 29-bit unit carries its own `id_bits`; the tool switches the adapter between the 11-bit and 29-bit protocols as it moves between units.

The 27 units are every addressed row of the CanZE ZOE_Ph2 ECU file, each also present in the ddt4all address table. Treat every row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering.

The S-GW3 security gateway is listed and nothing read states what it filters; units behind it may return no answer, which the tool reports as no response, not as absent.

Session: CanZE gives 0x03 for 21 units, 0xC0 for five (airbag, battery charger, INV-ME, USM, VSP) and 0x00 for the IDM. No one session is common and 0xC0 is not one the guard permits, so the profile opens the default session, 0x01; unconfirmed on a car.

Security gateway: a Renault security gateway is reported on recent cars, so a silent unit may be filtered rather than absent, and the tool reports a silent unit as no response, not as absent. A ddt4all issue (cedricp/ddt4all issue 404, Clio V, 2020) reports reads working through the OBD socket with writes blocked by a central gateway, and vendor pages (a Delphi article on a Renault Arkana, a Hella Gutmann page) say that fault codes and parameters can be read without unlocking it; none of them says which units a locked gateway hides from a read.
name: renault-zoe-ph2
description: Renault Zoe phase 2 (from 2019), UDS over mixed 11-bit and 29-bit CAN, address plan from CanZE and ddt4all

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.
